newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRADFORD LAUNCH CRIMINAL ACTION OVER INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRADFORD LAUNCH CRIMINAL ACTION OVER INJURY.

text.p: Bradford City launched criminal proceedings against Huddersfield Town defender Kevin Gray on Thursday over a tackle which left record signing Gordon Watson with a double fracture of his right leg last weekend.
The division one side became the first professional club in Britain to institute criminal action against a player.

Bradford's lawyer Michael Shepherd said doctors expected Watson, signed for a club record 550,000 pounds ($901,000) from Southampton just three weeks ago, to be out of the game for at least eight months.

"He will have to have at least one more operation,'' Shepherd said. "The surgeon has already inserted a six-inch plate with seven screws into his leg and Gordon is still in considerable pain. He is having great difficulty in coming to terms with his uncertain future.''
Bradford allege that Gray was guilty of causing Watson grevious bodily harm during the 1-1 league draw at Bradford on Saturday. The club have also launched a civil action for damages.
